analysis:
Examined both BASE excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (3593–4073) and the bounded patch. The visible edits exempt Gemma 4 from tensor-parallel-first ordering in favor of predicted speed and rename a referenced projection implementation while retaining its Qwen alias. Neither establishes a security regression. The surrounding BASE documents existing owner-only, build-scoped telemetry; load agreements; authenticated collectives; memory admission; tenant-partitioned caches; media bounds and digest agreement; and cancellation/token-credit behavior. These are existing contracts, not newly verified controls. Relevant threats include T-007/T-027 (output and model integrity), T-008 (fail-closed encryption), T-010 (cancellation), T-028/T-041 (residual data and cache isolation), T-050 (media plaintext), and T-053/T-054 (authorization/build binding). No visible edit changes credentials, attestation, billing, or plaintext handling.
Coverage is limited: the patch truncates at the new Gemma foundation heading, and HEAD 4037–4240 is not supplied here. Integration must examine that new section and corresponding runtime changes for shard/artifact verification, peer agreement, bounded allocations, authenticated transport, and preservation of coordinator-authored cache scope and encrypted SSD protections under T-041. The BASE GLM RAM-cache and numerical-qualification descriptions are pre-existing and are not findings against this PR. Missing HEAD/runtime evidence prevents a conclusion about the new Gemma execution surface; documentation alone does not establish implementation or activation.
